summary.headline: Emmvee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 1,555 crore, EBITDA margin 35%, PAT INR 380 crore (+103% YoY); order book 9.9 GW.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 1,555 crore (+51% YoY, down QoQ), with EBITDA of INR 548.1 crore (+56% YoY, -4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin of 35% versus 33% in Q4 FY26. PAT was INR 380.3 crore, helped by finance costs falling to INR 11.1 crore from INR 53.1 crore a year earlier. Module and cell production both hit record quarterly levels, with cell utilisation up to 83%, and order book rose to 9.9 GW after 1,484 MW of inflows. Management reiterated stable EBITDA per watt (module about INR 2.5/W, cell INR 6.0-6.5/W) and a 6 GW TOPCon cell and module expansion on schedule.

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: Production 970 MW (vs 635 MW in Q1 FY26, +53% YoY; 952 MW in Q4 FY26). Effective module utilisation 45% (vs 44% in both Q1 FY26 and Q4 FY26). DCR share of sales above 50%; module EBITDA about INR 2-2.5/W non-DCR and INR 8.5-9/W DCR per management.

segments.name: Solar cells
segments.commentary: Production 454 MW (vs 360 MW in Q1 FY26, +26% YoY; 428 MW in Q4 FY26). Cell utilisation 83% (vs 68% in Q1 FY26, 79% in Q4 FY26). Merchant cell sales rose sharply QoQ, described as the highest in company history; cell EBITDA about INR 6-6.5/W.

guidance_outlook: Targeting approximately INR 2,400 crore of EBITDA by close of FY27.

6 GW integrated TOPCon cell and module expansion: module line commissioning by December 2026, cell line by March 2027; total project cost about INR 5,500 crore (hard costs about INR 4,600 crore), debt of about INR 3,300 crore tied up at under 8%, about 60% of hard-cost orders placed.
Post-expansion capacity to reach about 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end FY27.

Backward integration into ingot and wafer: 9 GW in two phases (5 GW in FY29, 4 GW in FY30), timing subject to ALMM List 3 clarity and market conditions; capex mainly from internal accruals. Commissioning mid-CY2028 per management.
EBITDA per watt expected to stay stable; non-DCR module mix expected to be higher than DCR over next few quarters.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity: 10.3 GW modules and 2.94 GW TOPCon cells.
Management expects about 7+ GW of orders to be executed over the next 18 months.
Cell peak utilisation seen at about 85-90% and already close to that; module peak utilisation about 65%.
Transition of cell capacity to G12R under way, partially converted; effective cell capacity to rise even if utilisation % is similar.
Module utilisation in base case expected at similar levels (about 45%) in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Order inflow Q1 FY27 of 1,484 MW; order book 9.9 GW vs 9.4 GW at end FY26; DCR share of order book rising but non-DCR still significant.
Realisation for non-DCR module about 15-16 cents/W in Q4; a small increase of about INR 1/W in DCR realisation this quarter per management.
Sales are priced in USD across rooftop, KUSUM and C&I segments per management, which partly offsets input-cost moves.
C&I order inflows started after 1 June; supply to be expected later in FY27. DCR demand expected to strengthen progressively during FY27 with ALMM List 2 (effective June 2026).

Management said silver paste imports are subject to DGFT pre-approval; approvals received in 3-4 days so far, with about three months of inventory applied for, and no pricing premium versus earlier levels.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per watt trend for DCR and non-DCR modules?
qa_highlights.answer: Both DCR and non-DCR EBITDA spreads were in line with Q4 FY26 and are expected to remain stable.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin per watt trend and DCR mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided on EBITDA per watt: about INR 2.5/W for modules and INR 6.0-6.5/W for cells, similar to Q4. DCR share of sales was over 50%, including both modules and cells; future mix to be more non-DCR but DCR inventories will be used.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost fall 18-19% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a healthier DCR mix and higher internal cell consumption plus merchant cell sales; said this is mix-dependent and not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory position at quarter end?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 74.25 crore added to finished goods; management expects the strong order book to liquidate inventory, and raw material stock was deliberately raised due to geopolitical risk.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DCR module shortage in Karnataka real and what about run-rate increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Emmvee is equipped for phased ALMM rollout and ALMM List 3 discussions have begun; it expects cell production run-rate to rise further in coming quarters before new capacity arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per watt benefit from backward integration and utilisation gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the benefit is visible in absolute EBITDA and mix, not in blended per-watt numbers, because of efficiency gains that offset raw material headwinds.

risks_watch: Commissioning schedule of the 6 GW expansion (module Dec 2026, cell Mar 2027) and ramp-up of utilisation.
ALMM List 2 and List 3 implementation timing and DCR demand; reports of C&I players seeking deadline relief in Karnataka were not directly addressed.
Silver import licensing via DGFT and commodity-linked input price moves; management says pass-through is handled through value engineering and USD-linked selling prices.
Finished goods inventory build (INR 74.25 crore) and whether it unwinds in coming quarters.
Sustainability of stable EBITDA per watt if non-DCR share rises and C&I market shifts toward DCR cells.
Funding and execution of the proposed 9 GW ingot and wafer facility, with capex to be funded mostly by internal accruals.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on results and order book, but guarded on margin outlook: management repeatedly declined to give volume or gross margin guidance and framed margins as dependent on mix and market conditions.
key_quotes: Operationally, this was our best quarter so far.
Our order book further strengthened to 9.9 gigawatt, supported by fresh order inflows and approximately 1.5 gigawatt.
We are targeting approximately INR 2,400 crore of an EBITDA by the close of FY27.
So making that reasonable return even with lower utilization is rather better than making a higher utilization and lower margin.
